review_state: production rev 1 - M1, awaiting owner look review
purpose: Creature antler part (PROPOSED): a deer's branched antler, a ridged beam from a furred pedicle and knobbly burr curving up and back with four forward tines (mirrored at bake for the left).

textures.name: T_PartAntlerBranched_Albedo
textures.packing: greyscale albedo detail (baked AO darkens crevices), times each material's base colour

textures.name: T_PartAntlerBranched_ORM
textures.packing: R occlusion, G roughness, B metallic

handles.meaning: the antler 25% longer above the burr

part_rules.handles_note: The keys are on AntlerBranched (beam and tines); the pedicle (AntlerBranchedPedicle) stays put under the burr.

reduction.method: Blender collapse decimation within a surface tolerance; full-detail shading baked to the normal map

review_notes.gate1_shape: pass: from the side a deer's antler - a ridged beam rising from a furred pedicle through a knobbly burr ring, sweeping up and back and turning forward at the top, with brow, bez and trez tines reaching forward and up; from behind the crown tine forks inward off the beam and the brow tine angles in, so it branches from every side (0.15 x 0.167 x 0.35 m). H1_Length, H2_Spread and H3_Sweep move everything above the burr without tearing. In a scratch geometry preview the first draft was a thin straight stick whose stubby tines all pointed forward.
review_notes.gate2_materials: pass: two finishes - antler bone with gutters along the beam, pearled knobs toward the base and pale cream, smoother tips on every tine and the beam's end (a per-vertex Tip weight baked into the albedo; in mat_side the tine tips sample about 1.4 x the mid-beam's brightness, a moderate contrast), over short brown fur on the pedicle. The first bake read as turned wood (even tan, grain streaks) and the second hid the tips (beam already near white).
review_notes.gate3_neutral_light: pass: under the neutral white rig the gutters and burr knobs read by grazing light, the pedicle's fur stays brown without crushing, no clipping on the pale tips.
review_notes.gate4_godot: unverified: not yet seen in the creature editor (more_parts_shots.gd)

provenance: Authored procedurally in Blender by tools/blender/make_more_creature_parts.py, with helpers from tools/blender/make_creature_parts.py; no external or generated meshes. Textures baked in Blender from procedural shaders.
